correctness.rationale: Defines the Petersen graph explicitly as the pair-Kneser graph and the cap-b addition/removal adjacency. The proof checks the exact forest edge bound, classifies the 20 minimum stars, partitions all 140 feasible four-sets into 125 star-supersets and 15 four-cycles, and excludes precisely 12 nonstar five-cycles from the 252 candidates at cardinality five. It derives the 140 and 980 TAR transitions and gives explicit geodesics matching the |S△T| lower bound for every minimum pair (including disjoint stars). The two independently constructed Petersen graph models exhaustively test every candidate subset up to five and all 79,800 unordered pairs of the 400-state cap-five graph. Their source paths are embedded and both programs were run successfully; all advertised eccentricities and 120 diameter pairs are directly checked. Finite exhaustive proof applies only to this ten-vertex graph.

value.rationale: The capped-FVS reconfiguration question is mathematically motivated by whether optimal cycle-breaking vertex deletions can be shifted while preserving acyclicity. On the highly symmetric Petersen graph the optimum-only exchange graph is fragmented; its first two feasible budgets exhibit a sharp change, with 15 structurally characterized frozen four-cycles at budget four and detour-free shortest paths between all optima at budget five. Full-state eccentricity being exactly 8/9/10 by deletion-set cardinality, plus exact 120 extremal pairs, gives a natural complete finite metric invariant rather than an arbitrary table slice. Although the existence of a budget-five connection and original optima have antecedents, the exact geodesic and metric classification is substantive and not entailed by them.
